es: Ofrecer retroalimentación tras una derrota: reconocer un esfuerzo concreto, señalar una crítica específica y cerrar con el siguiente paso como pregunta de coaching.

teaching.en: I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed, because we all wanted this final so much.
teaching.es: Sé que la derrota duele y que tienen todo el derecho a sentirse decepcionados, porque todos queríamos tanto esta final.
teaching.explanationEs: Empieza reconociendo la emoción: así te escuchan antes de oír la crítica.
segments: I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to
feel disappointed, because we all wanted this final so much.
teaching.audioText: I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed, because we all wanted this final so much.

teaching.en: Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half, and I want us to learn from what worked.
teaching.es: A pesar de la derrota, estoy orgulloso de cómo defendieron en la segunda parte, y quiero que aprendamos de lo que funcionó.
teaching.explanationEs: Despite + sustantivo (sin of); proud of + el esfuerzo concreto.
segments: Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the
second half, and I want us to learn from what worked.
teaching.audioText: Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half, and I want us to learn from what worked.

teaching.en: However, we lost the ball too often in the middle, and that is a fixable problem, not a disaster.
teaching.es: Sin embargo, perdimos el balón demasiadas veces en el medio, y ese es un problema que tiene arreglo, no un desastre.
teaching.explanationEs: However + coma: una crítica concreta y limitada a una sola cosa.
segments: However, we lost the ball too often in the middle,
and that is a fixable problem, not a disaster.
teaching.audioText: However, we lost the ball too often in the middle, and that is a fixable problem, not a disaster.

teaching.en: After this setback, what will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday, and what could each of us try first?
teaching.es: Tras este contratiempo, ¿qué haría falta para recuperarnos el próximo sábado, y qué podría intentar primero cada uno?
teaching.explanationEs: Pregunta de coaching que proyecta el siguiente paso.
segments: After this setback, what will it take for us to bounce
back next Saturday, and what could each of us try first?
teaching.audioText: After this setback, what will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday, and what could each of us try first?

teaching.en: This was a tough result, but you deserve credit for your effort, because nobody on the pitch stopped running.
teaching.es: Fue un resultado duro, pero merecen reconocimiento por su esfuerzo, porque nadie en el campo dejó de correr.
teaching.explanationEs: Deserve credit for: reconocer el esfuerzo aunque se pierda.
segments: This was a tough result, but you deserve credit for
your effort, because nobody on the pitch stopped running.
teaching.audioText: This was a tough result, but you deserve credit for your effort, because nobody on the pitch stopped running.

teaching.en: There is still room for improvement in how we defend corners, but the setback is temporary and the season is long.
teaching.es: Todavía hay margen de mejora en cómo defendemos los córners, pero el contratiempo es temporal y la temporada es larga.
teaching.explanationEs: Setback: un problema temporal; ayuda a poner la derrota en perspectiva.

prompt.es: ¿Qué frase reconoce la emoción del equipo antes de empezar a criticar?

choices.text: I know the defeat hurts, and you have every right to feel disappointed.
We lost because you did not follow the plan that we agreed.
It was only a game, so nobody should feel disappointed about it today.

feedback.es: Solo la frase sobre el dolor de la derrota reconoce la emoción sin negarla ni culpar.

hint.es: Busca la que nombra lo que siente el equipo sin negarlo.

prompt.es: Completa: «Sin embargo, perdimos el balón demasiadas veces en el medio.»

feedback.es: However introduce la crítica concreta después del reconocimiento; va seguido de coma.

hint.es: Es el conector de contraste que empieza por H.

origin.text: The coach does not want to hide the truth, so she adds one limited criticism: ___, we lost the ball too often in the middle.

prompt.es: Ordena: «A pesar de la derrota, estoy orgulloso de cómo defendieron.»

answer.text: Despite the defeat I am proud of how you defended

feedback.es: Despite va seguido de sustantivo (the defeat) y proud lleva of en su complemento.

hint.es: Empieza por Despite y termina con la acción que se reconoce.

prompt.es: Escucha la charla y elige cómo abre la entrenadora su intervención.

choices.text: By pointing out the mistake that cost the match.
By recognising how the players feel about the loss.
By praising the captain for the goals that she scored.

feedback.es: Empieza con la emoción («the defeat hurts»); la crítica llega después con However.

origin.audio: The final whistle went, and the players sat in silence. The coach sat in front of them. I know the defeat hurts, she said, and you have every right to feel disappointed. Then she looked at the captain. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. However, we lost the ball too often in the middle, and that is fixable. She paused. What will it take for us to bounce back next Saturday? Nobody answered, but a few players were already nodding.

prompt.es: Con la misma charla, elige qué sugiere que algunos jugadores asientan.

choices.text: They agree that the coach was unfair to the captain in the second half.
They believe that the defeat was nobody's fault.
They accept the challenge and start thinking about the next match.

feedback.es: Nadie responde, pero asentir indica que la pregunta les hace pensar en cómo recuperarse.

prompt.es: Escribe un reconocimiento concreto y una crítica con However.

answer.text: I am proud of how fast you attacked. However, we left too much space at the back.
accepted: I am proud of how fast you attacked. However, we left too much space at the back.
I'm proud of your speed in attack; however, we left too much space behind us.

feedback.es: La frase combina un reconocimiento específico con una crítica concreta introducida por however.

origin.text: Tu equipo perdió 3-2. Escribe una frase que reconozca un esfuerzo concreto (la velocidad en el ataque) y continúe con however y una crítica concreta (dejaron demasiado espacio atrás).

prompt.es: Escribe la charla del entrenador tras la derrota.

answer.text:
Team, sit down for a moment. I know this defeat hurts, and it is fine to feel disappointed. I feel the same.
First, I want to say what I saw. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. Mia, your two tackles saved us three times, and Tom, you never stopped talking to the team. You deserve credit for that.
However, we lost the ball too often in the middle of the pitch, and that gave them the chance to score. It is only one thing, and it is fixable. One match does not decide our season.
So let me ask you: what would it take for us to keep the ball longer next Saturday? What could we try in training on Thursday? I would like to hear two ideas from each of you.
Go home, rest, and come back ready to learn. I believe in this team.
accepted:
Team, sit down for a moment. I know this defeat hurts, and it is fine to feel disappointed. I feel the same.
First, I want to say what I saw. Despite the defeat, I'm proud of how you defended in the second half. Mia, your two tackles saved us three times, and Tom, you never stopped talking to the team. You deserve credit for that.
However, we lost the ball too often in the middle of the pitch, and that gave them the chance to score. It is only one thing, and it is fixable. One match does not decide our season.
So let me ask you: what would it take for us to keep the ball longer next Saturday? What could we try in training on Thursday? I would like to hear two ideas from each of you.
Go home, rest, and come back ready to learn. I believe in this team.

Everyone, come here. I know how painful this defeat is, and I understand you are disappointed. I am too.
I want to start with what worked. I'm proud of how you supported each other during the last twenty minutes. Leo, your effort in defence was excellent, and Sara, you encouraged everybody until the final whistle.
However, we waited too long before we shot, and they blocked our chances easily. That is one concrete thing to improve, and it is not a disaster.
Now, what would help us to use the whole field next week? What is stopping us from looking for the right side? What could we try first on Tuesday? Think about it tonight, and tell me tomorrow.
It was a tough day, but you deserve to be proud of your effort. We will bounce back, and I will be with you on Saturday.

feedback.es: Una buena charla reconoce la emoción y dos esfuerzos concretos, hace una crítica específica con however y cierra con una pregunta de coaching.

origin.text: Tu equipo perdió 2–1 la final del barrio. Escribe la charla del entrenador (unas 200–250 palabras): reconoce la emoción y dos esfuerzos concretos (la defensa y el ánimo), señala una crítica concreta (por ejemplo, balones perdidos en el medio) y cierra con un plan formulado como pregunta de coaching.

prompt.es: Escucha el correo de la capitana y elige qué actitud muestra hacia la charla.

choices.text: She likes the talk but wants more concrete criticism too.
She values the talk, but she would prefer it to focus only on the positives.
She thinks the talk should have avoided any criticism.

feedback.es: La capitana agradece la charla pero pide más detalle sobre los errores: le gusta y exige concreción.

origin.audio: After the heavy defeat, the captain wrote an email to the coach. She said the talk had helped, but added that one sentence had stayed in her mind: It is only a setback. She explained that it had stopped her from blaming herself. In the same email she asked for more detail about the mistakes, because praise alone, she wrote, would not help the team improve.

prompt.es: Con el mismo correo, elige por qué menciona la frase «It is only a setback».

choices.text: Because it made her forget about the defeat entirely and stay calm.
Because it helped her stop blaming herself for the result.
Because it convinced her that nothing needed to change.

feedback.es: La frase la ayudó a dejar de culparse, pero ella sigue pidiendo detalles para mejorar: no olvidó la derrota.

prompt.es: Completa: «Una derrota es dura, pero los mejores equipos aprenden de ella.»

feedback.es: Learn from significa aprender de la experiencia; tras una derrota marca el paso de la queja al plan.

origin.text: Nobody enjoys losing a final. Even so, the best teams always ___ from a defeat, because it shows them exactly where to improve.

prompt.es: Escucha y elige qué contraste ilustra el relato entre las dos charlas.

choices.text: Criticism should always be avoided after a defeat.
Replacing the coach improves the results of the team.
Blame closes the conversation, while specific recognition opens it.

feedback.es: La primera charla culpa y silencia; la segunda reconoce, critica un hecho y pregunta, y los jugadores hablan.

origin.audio: After a two to one defeat, a coach said: That was a disaster, and you all know whose fault it was. The captain looked at the floor. A week later a different coach spoke to the same team after another loss: I'm proud of how you defended, however we lost the ball in the middle. What would help us keep it? The players talked about it all evening.

prompt.es: Lee la queja del jugador y elige la respuesta que reconoce, critica y propone un paso.

choices.text: You lost, but your second half was brave; however, we gave the ball away too often. What could we change?
You lost, so we have to work twice as hard from now on, and there will be no more excuses.
Nothing was good today, but the next match will surely be easier for all of us.

feedback.es: La respuesta combina reconocimiento (brave), una crítica concreta (ball away) y una pregunta de coaching.

origin.text: After the match a player says to the coach: We lost, so nothing we did today was good, and I am tired of trying.

prompt.es: Completa: «Dos derrotas seguidas duelen, pero este equipo puede recuperarse si aprende.»

feedback.es: Bounce back es recuperarse tras un contratiempo; la pregunta de coaching mira hacia adelante.

origin.text: Two defeats in a row hurt, but the season is long, and this team can ___ back if it learns.
